userStory: As a supplier, I want old listings to expire automatically so buyers do not request materials that are no longer available.
context: Surplus materials are often only available for a certain time. Old listings expire automatically to keep the marketplace fresh and avoid disappointed buyers.
acceptanceCriteria: Suppliers can set an expiry date when adding or editing a material listing.
When the expiry date passes, the system marks the item as 'Expired' and takes it out of buyer search results.
Expired materials will not appear in search or matching, but any existing approved reservation remains valid.
Suppliers can easily renew an expired listing by picking a new future date.
We send a friendly email reminder 7 days before an item expires so you can renew it if needed.

userStory: As a buyer, I want to search for materials by keyword or category so that I can quickly find what I need.
context: Buyers use search to discover available materials. Results only show checked, available materials and update smoothly.
acceptanceCriteria: Search matches material names and description words, and handles uppercase, lowercase, and minor spelling differences.
Buyers can filter by one or more material categories, and the list updates instantly without reloading the page.
Search only shows Verified, in-stock materials that have not expired.
If no materials match, a friendly message says 'No materials match your search' and offers a 'Clear Filters' button.
Results are organized into easy-to-browse pages of 20 items, and you can share your search link with teammates.
comments: Search by name, category filters, pagination, and empty state completed. Quality and stock checks apply to all search branches.

userStory: As a buyer, I want to find materials near my location so that we can save on transport time and costs.
context: Finding materials close to your site saves transport costs and reduces carbon emissions. You can easily filter by distance or city.
acceptanceCriteria: Every listing clearly shows pickup city, state, and country.
Buyers can filter by city and choose a distance radius: 25 km, 50 km, 100 km, or 250 km from their site.
When a location filter is selected, materials are sorted with the closest items first, showing distance in kilometers.
Listings without location coordinates still appear in regular keyword search with the note 'Location not specified'.
If an unrecognised city is entered, a helpful message explains 'Please check your city or pin code' instead of showing a blank screen.
Your chosen location and distance remain saved as you browse through search results.

userStory: As a buyer, I want to enter my project needs so the system can match me with the right surplus materials.
context: Instead of searching manually, enter what material you need, how much you need, and when. The system will find the best matches for you.
acceptanceCriteria: Buyers can create a request with material category, needed quantity, needed-by date, and maximum distance.
The system matches verified, available listings that have enough stock to meet your needs.
Each matching item shows a simple match score (like 95% Match) and explains why (e.g., 'Right category, 15 km away, enough stock').
If no materials match your exact needs, the system offers helpful tips, like broadening your search distance or quantity.
You can save your project requirements and re-run them whenever new materials are added.

userStory: As a buyer, I want to request material from a supplier so they can hold stock for our project.
context: When you find what you need, submit a request. The supplier reviews it and reserves the stock for you upon approval.
acceptanceCriteria: Select any verified material and enter the quantity you need (up to the available amount).
Enter your planned reuse, needed-by date, whether you will pick it up or need delivery, and your contact person.
Submitting creates a request reference (like REQ-2026-00001) marked 'Waiting for Supplier Review', and alerts the supplier.
You cannot submit duplicate requests for the same material while your first request is pending.
Suppliers see your request right away on their dashboard with your organization name and requested quantity.
You can withdraw your request at any time before the supplier approves it.
Submitting a request does not lock stock until the supplier clicks 'Approve Request'.

userStory: As a supplier, I want to approve or reject buyer requests so I can manage who gets our surplus materials.
context: Suppliers review incoming requests. Approving a request puts the stock on hold so no one else can take it.
acceptanceCriteria: Suppliers can review request details: buyer organization, quantity needed, project use, and requested pickup date.
Clicking 'Approve Request' puts the requested quantity on hold (moves it from Available to Reserved) in one step.
If stock is no longer available when you click approve, the system clearly notifies you: 'Available stock has changed. Please review updated quantities.'
If you must reject a request, select a reason (e.g. 'Not enough stock' or 'Schedule conflict') and add a friendly note for the buyer.
Suppliers can offer a partial quantity if they don't have the full amount. The buyer receives a message to accept or decline.
Both buyer and supplier receive instant notifications and can view the request status timeline.
